predecessors.name: Kidarites
predecessors.text: Bactria (Tokharistan) and Transoxiana, the Kidarite country

successors.name: First Turkic Khaganate
successors.text: the Hephthalite land (Transoxiana, Sogdia, Bactria north of the Oxus, Khwarezm, Fergana) in the Göktürk 561 shape

successors.name: Turk Shahis (Kabul Shahi)
successors.text: Kabulistan, the Turk Shahi country of 561

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: the rest of the 555 shape, south of the Oxus, where the Hephthalite principalities were under Sasanian suzerainty

ledger.x: 450: the Hephthalites emerge on the northern Hindu Kush.
450: the Hephthalites begin to beat the Kidarites.
466: the Hephthalites take Transoxiana from the Kidarites.

479: Sogdia. 'By 479 the Hephthalites had conquered Sogdia and driven the Kidarites eastwards'; the page also has they 'may have conquered Sogdiana as early as 479 CE', that the Liang Zhigongtu 'seems to record that from around 479 CE, the Hephthalites occupied the region of Samarkand', and 'In 509, they captured…
484: Peroz I dies and Khorasan falls to the Hephthalites.
490: the Indian lands appear in the White Huns row.
557: Turks and Sasanians attack the Hephthalites.
560: the fighting ends with the empire destroyed 'around 560 CE'.
560: the northern Hephthalite land goes to the Turks.
560: Kabulistan goes to the Turk Shahis.

wars.name: Hephthalite-Kidarite wars
wars.outcome: The Hephthalites beat the Kidarites from the 450s; Peroz I, 'with their help', 'finally vanquished Kidarites in 466' (Kidarites page: Peroz 'reconquering Balkh' in 467); the Hephthalites took Transoxiana about 466 and Sogdia by 479, and the Kidarites withdrew…

wars.name: Peroz I's Hephthalite wars
wars.outcome: Peroz attacked in 474 and was ambushed and captured near Gurgan (ransomed by Zeno); a second campaign in the late 470s or early 480s ended in his capture again and a ransom of silver (his son Kavad hostage in 482); the third, in 484, ended in his death.

wars.name: Kavad I's eastern wars
wars.outcome: Kavad, who had returned in 498/9 with a Hephthalite army, went east against 'hostile Huns' in 503, took the Zundaber castle in 508, and 'by 513 had re-taken the region of Khorasan'.

wars.name: Hunnic wars (First and Second)
wars.outcome: Toramana reached the maximum extent about 500-515 and was defeated in 515 (Prakashadharma); Mihirakula's Second Hunnic War from 520 ended in defeat in 528 and 'c.

wars.name: Göktürk-Sasanian war against the Hephthalites
wars.outcome: The Hephthalite empire was destroyed 'around 560 CE'; the Turks took the land north of the Oxus and the Sasanians held suzerainty south of it.

certainty.note: Steppe and mountain frontiers throughout; no treaty line is dated by the pages.
